title: CI 33164294061 root-cause diagnosis
body: GitHub run https://github.com/xiaden/Universeity/actions/runs/33164294061 at commit a6b1a62 failed for multiple independent causes. Hosted logs/artifacts prove: unit job 1 failure from test_docker_compose_config_when_daemon_present because required HATCHET_COOKIE_SECRET was absent; Postgres job 14 failures = six multipart failures with Starlette assertion that python-multipart is not installed, six ffmpeg FileNotFoundError failures, one pg_dump FileNotFoundError at /usr/lib/postgresql/17/bin/pg_dump, one same Compose interpolation assertion; Docker job fails before startup at GHCR manifest request for ghcr.io/hatchet-dev/hatchet:v0.105.2 with denied, so all later readiness/E2E steps skipped. Code/design evidence shows product integration gap beyond environment: app.py imports/instantiates DurableDAGRunner, while ProductionDAGRunner is the Hatchet submission seam; existing dedicated live tests at test_hatchet_live.py:920-1006 use real-client shape but handoff also records defective recording-client tests with executor=None; worker extra is optional in pyproject and Dockerfile base install needs inspection. This is NEEDS_PLAN, not SIMPLE; R&D planning then Exec-Manager required. No code modified by debugger.

title: Plan J remains blocked by hosted evidence
body: Run 33164294061 confirms the Plan J dependency block recorded in exec-manager log L57: Docker startup fails at Hatchet GHCR image pull denial, PostgreSQL/unit environments miss required runtime dependencies and Compose secrets, and product Hatchet execution is not proven. Plan J phases 3-4 must not be marked complete; R&D design and implementation planning are required before Exec-Manager.

title: CI-only hypothesis eliminated
body: For run 33164294061, hypothesis that the failure was only a test assertion regression is eliminated. Hosted evidence spans six multipart dependency failures, six missing ffmpeg failures, one missing pg_dump failure, two Compose secret interpolation failures, GHCR Hatchet image denial before startup, and a distinct production API runner mismatch. Lint and strict mypy passing cannot establish runtime/deployment correctness.

title: Hosted netns recurrence has two root causes
body: Read-only RCA from GitHub runs 33228376245, 33228084721, 33226431905, and 33226227591 plus current tree. Runs 33228084721 and 33226431905 show exact daemon error `Error response from daemon: bind-mount /proc/<transient-pid>/ns/net -> /var/run/docker/netns/<id>: no such file or directory` while starting `umd-sandbox-runner-1`; random PID/netns IDs and daemon origin identify hosted Docker/Moby namespace lifecycle race/runner limit, not Compose DNS/topology. Latest run 33228376245 starts db/api/worker/Hatchet and fails first at Docker E2E step 8 with `sandbox-runner=restarting`; downloaded diag-final/log-sandbox-runner.txt proves custom seccomp denies `statx`/`fsmount` (`operation not permitted`), while `getcwd() failed: Operation not permitted` and `/usr/local/bin/docker-entrypoint.sh: 24: Cannot fork` repeat. `compose-ps.txt` shows API/db/worker/engine/dashboard running, migrate/admin exited 0, sandbox restarting. Current workflow has bounded netns retry and reconciliation, but must not treat all failures as transient. Plan K P3-S3 (plan lines 51-62) requires full moby default syscall surface plus bwrap additions; Task/plan require complete native Compose topology, no skips/DinD/socket mounts/fake readiness. Safe remediation: retain native topology/gates; use narrowly matching bounded retry and fresh reconciliation for exact daemon error; fix seccomp from complete moby default baseline plus required bwrap syscalls, retaining nonprivileged controls; verify sandbox env and real execution. Required proof is pushed-SHA hosted evidence: no daemon bind-mount errors/restart loops, exact service state/inspect, zero seccomp EPERM, all live/boundary JUnit tests executed with skipped=0, real workflow registration/callback rows and HTTP/restart/persistence PASS markers. No code changed.

title: Netns recurrence remains unclassified at daemon/topology boundary
body: Read-only diagnosis for Plan K hosted runs 33226227591 (R10), 33227518543 (R15), 33228084721 (R16), and 33228376245 (R17), with mandated artifacts and current tree. Direct /proc/<pid>/ns/net bind-mount errors support a hosted Docker/Moby namespace lifecycle race hypothesis; R15 separately confirms a workflow orchestration defect because compose up returned zero while required services remained Created, addressed by post-up ps -a -q/state reconciliation. No custom networks or network_mode in deploy/compose.yaml and split topology booted in R11, so Compose architecture is not proven causal. R16/R17 independently prove sandbox seccomp/bwrap incompatibility (statx/fsmount/getcwd/vfork EPERM), distinct from netns. Classification: NEEDS_PLAN for the release-gate investigation, with recurrence mechanism INCONCLUSIVE until per-run daemon/runtime/timing evidence is captured. Preserve full split Hatchet, mandatory hosted gates, no skips/stubs/fake readiness, no host networking/socket/DinD/Lite/second scheduler. No files edited.

title: Sandbox seccomp is independent from netns recurrence
body: R16 33228084721 (statx/fsmount EPERM) and R17 33228376245 (getcwd/vfork EPERM) plus deploy/security/sandbox-seccomp.json and src/umd/security/bwrap.py establish a separate sandbox startup/profile incompatibility. It explains sandbox crash/restart, not the Docker /proc/<pid>/ns/net bind-mount disappearance; do not use it as proof of netns causation.

title: Compose topology causality not established
body: Across deploy/compose.yaml and hosted runs R10 33226227591, R11 33226431905, R15 33227518543, no custom networks or network_mode are present; the full split topology booted in R11. Therefore a Compose topology redesign cannot be confirmed as the cause of /proc/<pid>/ns/net disappearance. Retain as an open possibility only pending daemon/runtime/timing evidence.

title: Hosted live submissions queued but unassigned
body: Run 33229130339 artifacts show real Hatchet submissions reached the engine: diag-final/umd-dump.sql contains 46 v1_tasks_olap_20260829 rows and 46 v1_runs_olap_20260829 rows, including live-dup/live-shape/live-universe payloads, all readable_status=QUEUED. It also contains 9 Workflow rows, 10 WorkflowVersion rows including exact umd-* actions, and Worker umd-worker tenant heartbeat 02:32:15-02:38:28 with isActive=true, isPaused=false, sdkVersion=1.38.1; WorkerAssignEvent data is empty and worker log only says waiting for tasks. UMD stage_run/job audit/StageCompleted tables remain empty. This narrows failure from submission/API/DB mismatch to Hatchet scheduler assignment/worker action registration/queue eligibility; exact SDK action hash/queue records still under analysis.

title: Durable requirement mismatch visible in hosted task rows
body: Hosted dump v1_task_20260829 rows show is_durable=f for all submitted tasks. Product src/umd/jobs/hatchet.py HatchetWorkerFactory.start line 427 uses real SDK client.task(name=wf_name), not client.durable_task; SDK Task.to_proto emits is_durable from decorator, and Hatchet.worker resolves standard/durable slots based on workflow tasks. This is an evidence-backed contract mismatch with Task/Plan K durable async requirement, but by itself does not yet prove why standard tasks were left QUEUED: worker registration has standard slot_config expected and action names appear exact. Must verify whether this non-durable registration is the dispatch blocker or merely violates the durable requirement; do not conflate.

title: Root cause: hosted JWT minted for internal tenant with no scheduler partition
body: Run 33229130339 / Docker 99038602321 exact root cause: validation.yml lines 277-285 discovers the first Hatchet tenant with ORDER BY "createdAt" LIMIT 1, which is the system `internal` tenant, not the user `Default` tenant. diag-final/umd-dump.sql proves internal tenant 8d420720-ef03-41dc-9c73-1c93f276db97 has schedulerPartitionId=NULL and workerPartitionId=NULL, while Default tenant 707d0855-80ab-4e1f-a156-f1c4546cbf52 has both partitions populated. APIToken `default` and the active `umd-worker`, nine workflows, and all 45 v1_task/v1_queue_item rows are tenant 8d420...; SchedulerPartition/Controller/TenantWorkerPartition heartbeats exist only for Default's assigned partitions. Thus engine persisted submissions and worker registration but scheduler had no tenant partition assigned for the token's internal tenant, so no assignment/runtime/event/callback and UMD stage rows stayed zero. Root cause is hosted tenant provisioning/JWT selection, not product runner, DB DSN, callback, token validity, or run_workflow shape. Remediation: select the actual user/default tenant deterministically after quickstart (e.g. query tenant with non-null schedulerPartitionId/workerPartitionId and fail if not exactly one; or use the tenant id returned/created by setup), mint JWT for that tenant, then assert token tenant == worker/workflow tenant and tenant partition IDs are non-null before live tests. Preserve real gates; no skips/doubles/fake readiness. Falsifier: rerun exact pair with JWT for Default tenant; dump must show submitted task tenant = 707d..., scheduler/worker partition IDs non-null, queue items transition to assigned/running and worker logs show callback; if still queued, investigate next-level scheduler pair issue.

title: Observation: worker readiness gate misses tenant scheduler partition
body: The hosted readiness contract validates only worker log text (`.github/scripts/wait-for-worker.sh`) and registration metadata, not that the JWT's tenant has scheduler/worker partitions or that a queued task is assigned. validation.yml tenant discovery chooses first Tenant row by createdAt, which is the system internal tenant. This lets real registration pass while scheduler eligibility is impossible. A fail-closed preflight must validate selected tenant partition IDs before minting/starting live gate.

title: Eliminated: DB mismatch, SDK submission shape, callback failure
body: Run 33229130339 evidence eliminates three hypotheses. DB mismatch: diag-final/umd-dump.sql shows same tenant-scoped Hatchet workflows, worker, tasks, queue items and empty UMD tables in shared db; Compose API/worker use db:5432/umd and host live_db uses published 127.0.0.1:5432/umd. Submission API mismatch: pinned SDK 1.38.1 AdminClient.run_workflow accepts (workflow_name, input, options=...), so two positional args in src/umd/jobs/hatchet.py::_real_submit_workflow_run are valid. Callback/executor failure: 45 tasks remain QUEUED with no v1_task_runtime/StepRun/WorkerAssignEvent/worker_id and worker log has no callback/error; execution never reached _make_handler or DurableStageExecutor. Registration/token/host primary hypothesis also eliminated as sole cause: dump has active umd-worker, SDK 1.38.1, heartbeat, dispatcher/listener, 9 _ActionToWorker links, exact action IDs; token was accepted for registration. Readiness helper is weak but not causal.
